title: Great Indian Bustard Chicks Enter Rewilding Tunnel in Rajasthan
summary: Three chicks of the Great Indian Bustard were released on 26 July 2026 into a specially designed rewilding tunnel at the Godawan Conservation Centre in Ramdevra, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. The birds, identified as R9, R10 and R11, are one month ...

blocks.content: Three chicks of the Great Indian Bustard were released on 26 July 2026 into a specially designed rewilding tunnel at the Godawan Conservation Centre in Ramdevra, Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. The birds, identified as R9, R10 and R11, are one month old and include two males and one female.

items: The chicks will remain under continuous CCTV surveillance for about four months.
Food will be supplied externally without direct human interaction.
The tunnel is intended to help the birds develop foraging behaviour and desert adaptation.
The facility supports safe rehabilitation before release into open habitat.
The Great Indian Bustard is listed as critically endangered on the IUCN Red List.
Rajasthan is the main stronghold of the Great Indian Bustard in India.
The species is protected under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
Desert National Park is located in the Jaisalmer and Barmer districts of Rajasthan.
